In [[geometry]], the '''Hessian polyhedron''' is a [[regular complex polytope|regular complex polyhedron]] <sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub>, {{CDD|3node_1|3|3node|3|3node}}, in <math>\mathbb{C}^3</math>.  It has 27 vertices, 72 <sub>3</sub>{} edges, and 27 [[Möbius–Kantor polygon|<sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub>]] faces. It is self-dual. 

[[Harold Scott MacDonald Coxeter|Coxeter]] named it after [[Ludwig Otto Hesse]] for sharing the ''[[Hessian configuration]]'' <math>\left [\begin{smallmatrix} 9&4\\3&12 \end{smallmatrix}\right ]</math> or (9<sub>4</sub>12<sub>3</sub>), 9 points  lying by threes on twelve lines, with four lines through each point.<ref>Coxeter, Complex Regular polytopes, p.123</ref>

Its [[complex reflection group]] is <sub>3</sub>[3]<sub>3</sub>[3]<sub>3</sub> or {{CDD|3node|3|3node|3|3node}}, order 648, also called a [[Hessian group]]. It has 27 copies of {{CDD|3node|3|3node}}, order 24, at each vertex. It has 24 order-3 reflections. Its [[Coxeter number]] is 12, with degrees of the fundamental invariants 3, 6, and 12, which can be seen in projective symmetry of the polytopes.

The [[Witting polytope]], <sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub>, {{CDD|3node_1|3|3node|3|3node|3|3node}} contains the Hessian polyhedron as [[cell (geometry)|cells]] and [[vertex figure]]s.

It has a real representation as the [[2 21 polytope|''2<sub>21</sub>'' polytope]], {{CDD|nodes_10r|3ab|nodes|split2|node|3|node}}, in 6-dimensional space, sharing the same 27 vertices. The 216 edges in ''2<sub>21</sub>'' can be seen as the 72 <sub>3</sub>{} edges represented as 3 simple edges.

== Coordinates==
Its 27 vertices can be given coordinates in <math>\mathbb{C}^3</math>:  for (&lambda;, &mu; = 0,1,2).
:(0,&omega;<sup>&lambda;</sup>,−&omega;<sup>&mu;</sup>)
: (−&omega;<sup>&mu;</sup>,0,&omega;<sup>&lambda;</sup>)
: (&omega;<sup>&lambda;</sup>,−&omega;<sup>&mu;</sup>,0) 

where <math>\omega = \tfrac{-1+i\sqrt3}{2}</math>.

{| class=wikitable width=320 align=right
|[[File:Complex polyhedron 3-3-3-3-3-one-blue-face.png|160px]]<BR>Hessian polyhedron  with triangular 3-edges outlined as black edges, with one face outlined as blue.
|[[File:Complex_polyhedron_3-3-3-3-3-one-blue-van_oss_polygon.png|160px]]<BR>One of 12 Van oss polygons, [[3-3_duoprism#Related_complex_polygons|<sub>3</sub>{4}<sub>2</sub>]], in the Hessian polyhedron
|}

Its symmetry is given by <sub>3</sub>[3]<sub>3</sub>[3]<sub>3</sub> or {{CDD|3node|3|3node|3|3node}}, order 648.<ref>Coxeter Regular Convex Polytopes, 12.5 The Witting polytope</ref> 

The [[Configuration (polytope)|configuration matrix]] for <sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub> is:<ref>Coxeter, Complex Regular polytopes, p.132</ref>
:<math>\left [\begin{smallmatrix}27&8&8\\3&72&3\\8&8&27\end{smallmatrix}\right ]</math>

The number of k-face elements ([[f-vector]]s) can be read down the diagonal. The number of elements of each k-face are in rows below the diagonal. The number of elements of each k-figure are in rows above the diagonal.

||8||8||BGCOLOR="#e0ffe0"|'''27'''||( )||L<sub>3</sub>/L<sub>2</sub> = 27*4!/4! = 27

The ''Hessian polyhedron'' can be seen as an alternation of {{CDD|node_1|4|3node|3|3node}}, {{CDD|node_h|4|3node|3|3node}} = {{CDD|label-33|nodes_10ru|split2|node|label3}}. This ''double Hessian polyhedron'' has 54 vertices, 216 simple edges, and 72 {{CDD|node_1|4|3node}} faces. Its vertices represent the union of the vertices {{CDD|3node_1|3|3node|3|3node}} and its dual {{CDD|3node|3|3node|3|3node_1}}.

Its [[complex reflection group]] is <sub>3</sub>[3]<sub>3</sub>[4]<sub>2</sub>, or {{CDD|3node|3|3node|4|node}}, order 1296. It has 54 copies of {{CDD|3node|3|3node}}, order 24, at each vertex. It has 24 order-3 reflections and 9 order-2 reflections. Its [[coxeter number]] is 18, with degrees of the fundamental invariants 6, 12, and 18 which can be seen in projective symmetry of the polytopes.

[[Harold Scott MacDonald Coxeter|Coxeter]] noted that the three complex polytopes {{CDD|3node_1|3|3node|3||3node}}, {{CDD|node_1|4|3node|3||3node}}, {{CDD|3node_1|3|3node|4|node}} resemble the real [[tetrahedron]] ({{CDD|node_1|3|node|3|node}}), [[cube]] ({{CDD|node_1|4|node|3|node}}), and [[octahedron]] ({{CDD|node_1|3|node|4|node}}). The Hessian is analogous to the tetrahedron, like the cube is a [[Compound of two tetrahedra|double tetrahedron]], and the octahedron as a rectified tetrahedron. In both sets the vertices of the first belong to two dual pairs of the second, and the vertices of the third are at the center of the edges of the second.<ref>Coxeter, Complex Regular Polytopes, p.127</ref> 

Its real representation 54 vertices are contained by two [[2_21 polytope|2<sub>21</sub>]] polytopes in symmetric configurations: {{CDD|nodes_10r|3ab|nodes|split2|node|3|node}} and {{CDD|nodes_01r|3ab|nodes|split2|node|3|node}}. Its vertices can also be seen in the dual polytope of [[1_22 polytope|1<sub>22</sub>]].

The [[rectification (geometry)|rectification]], {{CDD|3node|3|3node_1|3|3node}} doubles in symmetry as a regular complex polyhedron {{CDD|3node_1|3|3node|4|node}} with 72 vertices, 216 <sub>3</sub>{} edges, 54 <sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub> faces. Its vertex figure is <sub>3</sub>{4}<sub>2</sub>, and van oss polygon <sub>3</sub>{4}<sub>3</sub>. It is dual to the ''double Hessian polyhedron''.<ref>Coxeter, H. S. M., ''Regular Complex Polytopes'', second edition, Cambridge University Press, (1991). p.30 and p.47</ref>

It has a real representation as the [[1 22 polytope#Related complex polyhedron|1<sub>22</sub>]] polytope, {{CDD|nodes|3ab|nodes|split2|node|3|node_1}}, sharing the 72 vertices. Its 216 3-edges can be drawn as 648 simple edges, which is 72 less than 1<sub>22</sub>'s 720 edges.

|}
